# Captured from a real nginx, `server_tokens off;`, 2026-08-21.
#
#   nginx version: nginx/1.31.4 (Homebrew, arm64 macOS)
#   conf: worker_processes 1; server_tokens off; listen 8791; root html;
#
# These are the bytes `crates/aberp-portal-relay/src/nginx.rs` must
# reproduce EXACTLY on the un-knocked path. `{DATE}` is the only field
# that varies; everything else — status line, header ORDER, every
# Content-Length, the body down to its CRLFs — is pinned by
# `tests/nginx_indistinguishable.rs`.
#
# The capture procedure is in ADR-0115 §3.3 so a future reader can
# re-run it against a newer nginx rather than trusting this file.
#
# Header order is load-bearing: Server, Date, Content-Type,
# Content-Length, Connection. nginx emits exactly that, and a reordered
# set is a fingerprint even when every value matches.

[404] GET /nope HTTP/1.1 + Host + Connection: close
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 146\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>404 Not Found</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>404 Not Found</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

[404-keepalive] GET /nope HTTP/1.1 + Host (no Connection header)
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 146\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>404 Not Found</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>404 Not Found</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

[400] bad request-line ("NOT A VALID REQUEST LINE"), missing Host on
      HTTP/1.1, duplicate Host, space in the URI, malformed header
      name, and TLS ClientHello bytes sent to a plaintext port — all
      collapse to this one answer.
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 150\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>400 Bad Request</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>400 Bad Request</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

[405] FROBNICATE /nope HTTP/1.1 — a well-formed token that is not
      GET/HEAD/POST. Note it ECHOES keep-alive; it does not close.
HTTP/1.1 405 Not Allowed\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 150\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>405 Not Allowed</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>405 Not Allowed</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

[414] request line longer than the 8k large_client_header_buffers slot
HTTP/1.1 414 Request-URI Too Large\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 170\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>414 Request-URI Too Large</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>414 Request-URI Too Large</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

[505] HTTP/9.9 and HTTP/2.0 over a cleartext http1 listener
HTTP/1.1 505 HTTP Version Not Supported\r\nServer: nginx\r\nDate: {DATE}\r\nContent-Type: text/html\r\nContent-Length: 180\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n<html>\r\n<head><title>505 HTTP Version Not Supported</title></head>\r\n<body>\r\n<center><h1>505 HTTP Version Not Supported</h1></center>\r\n<hr><center>nginx</center>\r\n</body>\r\n</html>\r\n

# Behaviours pinned as assertions rather than byte captures
# (tests/nginx_indistinguishable.rs):
#
#   HEAD /nope       -> the 404 HEAD, Content-Length: 146, NO body.
#   GET /nope HTTP/1.0 without Host  -> 404, not 400. Host is only
#                                       mandatory on HTTP/1.1.
#   GET /nope HTTP/1.0               -> Connection: close by default.
#   GET /nope HTTP/1.0 + keep-alive  -> Connection: keep-alive.
#   Connection: KEEP-ALIVE           -> matched case-insensitively.
#   chunked request body             -> body drained, then the 404,
#                                       keep-alive preserved.
#   leading CRLFs before the line    -> skipped, then the 404.
#   bare-LF line endings             -> accepted, then the 404.
#   absolute-form target             -> 404 (not 400).
#   OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1               -> 400.
#   GET /nope with no HTTP version   -> HTTP/0.9: the 146-byte body
#                                       ALONE, no status line, no
#                                       headers, then close.
